chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Usury (riba) is two types: a usury that is eaten and a usury that is not eaten.
As for that which is eaten, it is your gift to a man, seeking from him a reward greater than it; that is the usury which is eaten.
And it is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever you give as usury, so that it may increase in the property of the people, it will not increase in the Presence of Allah.'
And as for that which is not eaten, it is the usury which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade and promised the Fire for.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the two types of usury (riba) according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between two types of usury (riba): one that is 'eaten' (consumed/lost spiritually), which refers to a gift given with the expectation of a greater return, and one that is 'not eaten', which is the specific usury forbidden by Allah and punished with Hellfire. The text cites Quran 30:39 to support the concept of riba that does not increase with God. This classification highlights the subtle distinction between social reciprocity that becomes exploitative and the formal interest-based transactions condemned in Sharia.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The interest are two (types) of interest – an interest which can be eaten and an interest which cannot be eaten.
So as for the interest which can be eaten, so it is a gift to the man. Seeking the Rewards from it is better than (eating) it. So that is the interest which can be eaten,
and these are the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [30:39] And whatever you give out as interest, so that it may increase in the property of the people, it will not increase in the Presence of Allah.
And as for that which cannot be eaten, so it is the interest which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from it, and Prepared the Fire upon it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar af-Yamaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Riba’ is of two kinds: One kind is that which is consumed and the other kind is not consumed.
The gift that one presents to someone in order to receive Thawab (rewards from Allah) is better. Of this kind is the Riba’ which is consumed
as it is mentioned in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ’The Riba’ in which you are involved so it increases in people’s property does not increase before Allah.’ [30:38]
The other kind of Riba’ is that which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has prohibited and has warned those involved in it with punishment in the fire.”
